words.gloss: of the gains of ally, money and land

hindi: संहित प्रयाण में मित्र, धन और भूमि के लाभों में से उत्तरोत्तर लाभ श्रेष्ठ है।
english: In a march in alliance, of the gains of ally, money and land, each succeeding gain [is] better.
notes: saṃhita-prayāṇa taken literally as a march made allied or joined; the text does not say with whom. hiraṇya = money (glossary 5.2). uttara.uttaraḥ read as the repeated compound 'each later one'. mitra-hiraṇya-bhūmi-lābhānām: lābha = acquisition (Book 7 chapter on acquisitions); the dvandva is of the three things acquired. Reviewer: lābha = gain (glossary 7.7, 7.10), not 'acquisition'.
lines_deva: संहित.प्रयाणे मित्र.हिरण्य.भूमि.लाभानाम् उत्तर.उत्तरो लाभः श्रेयान्
lines_iast: saṃhita.prayāṇe mitra.hiraṇya.bhūmi.lābhānām uttara.uttaro lābhaḥ śreyān

hindi: क्योंकि मित्र और धन भूमि के लाभ से होते हैं, मित्र धन के लाभ से।
english: For ally and money arise from the gain of land, ally from the gain of money.
notes: Second clause has no verb; bhavataḥ is understood. 'Arise' for bhavataḥ is literal 'become/come to be'.
lines_deva: मित्र.हिरण्ये हि भूमि.लाभाद् भवतः, मित्रं हिरण्य.लाभात्
lines_iast: mitra.hiraṇye hi bhūmi.lābhād bhavataḥ, mitraṃ hiraṇya.lābhāt

hindi: अथवा जो लाभ सिद्ध हुआ, शेष दोनों में से किसी एक को साधता है।
english: Or whichever gain, accomplished, accomplishes one of the remaining two.
notes: sādhayati (caus. √sādh) rendered 'accomplishes'; the sense 'brings about / secures' is the same. Hindi leaves the correlative unstated because the Sanskrit has no tad here (saḥ is absent).
lines_deva: यो वा लाभः सिद्धः शेषयोर् अन्यतरं साधयति
lines_iast: yo vā lābhaḥ siddhaḥ śeṣayor anyataraṃ sādhayati

words.gloss: having this as its beginning, and so on

hindi: “तुम और मैं मित्र प्राप्त करते हैं”, इस प्रकार आदि वाली सम-सन्धि है।
english: “You and I obtain an ally”, [that] which has this as its beginning is an equal treaty.

text_flags.why: possible: stray h for visarga (ādiḥ); the next word begins with s, and unit 5 reads evaṃ.ādir

notes: sama-sandhi = even treaty (glossary: sandhi = treaty; sama/viṣama = even/uneven as in 10.5). labhāvahe is a 1 du. present middle (the imperative would be labhāvahai). The closing iti of the quotation is carried by the quotation marks. Reviewer: sama/viṣama-sandhi = equal/unequal treaty (glossary 7.7), not 'even/uneven'.
lines_deva: "त्वं च-अहं च मित्रं लभावहे" इत्य् एवं.आदिध् सम.सन्धिः
lines_iast: "tvaṃ ca-ahaṃ ca mitraṃ labhāvahe" ity evaṃ.ādidh sama.sandhiḥ

words.gloss: having this as its beginning, and so on

hindi: “तुम मित्र”, इस प्रकार आदि वाली विषम-सन्धि है।
english: “You [are] an ally”, [that] which has this as its beginning is an unequal treaty.
notes: The quotation tvaṃ mitram has no verb; '[are]' is a bare copula. It could also be read 'you [obtain] an ally', or mitram as accusative, but the text gives no verb. The printed 'ādir viṣama' is regular sandhi for ādiḥ viṣama.
lines_deva: "त्वं मित्रम्" इत्य् एवं.आदिर् विषम.सन्धिः
lines_iast: "tvaṃ mitram" ity evaṃ.ādir viṣama.sandhiḥ

hindi: उन दोनों के विशेष लाभ से अतिसन्धि है।
english: From a special gain of those two, [there is] an outwitting treaty (atisandhi).
notes: atisandhi kept as the term (literally 'over-treaty'); the sense 'outwitting' follows from atisandhatte in the next unit (cf. glossary atisandhā = outwit). tayoḥ taken as 'of the two (treaties)'; locative 'in the two' is also possible. Verb not stated.
lines_deva: तयोर् विशेष.लाभाद् अतिसन्धिः
lines_iast: tayor viśeṣa.lābhād atisandhiḥ

hindi: किन्तु सम-सन्धि में जो उत्कृष्ट मित्र अथवा मित्र की कठिनाई में मित्र प्राप्त करता है, वह छल लेता है।
english: But in an equal treaty, he who obtains an excellent ally, or an ally in an ally's difficulty, outwits [the other].
notes: sampanna = literally 'endowed, accomplished'; 'excellent' chosen (cf. unit 38 sampannaṃ mitraṃ ṣaḍ-guṇam). The object of atisandhatte is not stated. The printed 'so 'tisandhatte' = saḥ atisandhatte.
lines_deva: सम.सन्धौ तु यः सम्पन्नं मित्रं मित्र.कृच्छ्रे वा मित्रम् अवाप्नोति सो ऽतिसन्धत्ते
lines_iast: sama.sandhau tu yaḥ sampannaṃ mitraṃ mitra.kṛcchre vā mitram avāpnoti so 'tisandhatte

hindi: क्योंकि आपत्ति सौहार्द की स्थिरता उत्पन्न करती है।
english: For adversity produces steadiness of friendship.
notes: The printed 'āpadd hi' (doubled d) is the edition's regular spelling for āpad hi (the same occurs in 'tadd hi', unit 9); not flagged.
lines_deva: आपद्द् हि सौहृद.स्थैर्यम् उत्पादयति
lines_iast: āpadd hi sauhṛda.sthairyam utpādayati

words.gram: n. nom. sg. pres. part. an-upa-√kṛ

hindi: मित्र की कठिनाई में भी नित्य, वश में न रहने वाला, अथवा अनित्य, वश में रहने वाला — “नित्य, वश में न रहने वाला श्रेष्ठ है, क्योंकि वह उपकार न करता हुआ भी अपकार नहीं करता,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: Even in an ally's difficulty, a constant, uncontrolled [ally] or an inconstant, controlled one — “The constant, uncontrolled [one] is better, for it does not harm even when not helping,” say the teachers.
notes: The first iti (after vā) closes the either-or question; it is not rendered, the dash marks it. No noun is stated in the quotation. avaśya = not under control (a-vaśya), not Hindi 'certainly'; vaśya = under control. 'tadd hi' is the edition's regular spelling for tad dhi/tad hi.
lines_deva: मित्र.कृच्छ्रे ऽपि नित्यम् अवश्यम् अनित्यं वश्यं वा-इति "नित्यम् अवश्यं श्रेयः, तद्द् हि अनुपकुर्वद् अपि न-अपकरोति" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: mitra.kṛcchre 'pi nityam avaśyam anityaṃ vaśyaṃ vā-iti "nityam avaśyaṃ śreyaḥ, tadd hi anupakurvad api na-apakaroti" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

hindi: वश में रहने वाला अनित्य श्रेष्ठ है।
english: The controlled, inconstant [one] [is] better.
notes: No noun is stated; '[one]' is understood (the ally).
lines_deva: वश्यम् अनित्यं श्रेयः
lines_iast: vaśyam anityaṃ śreyaḥ

hindi: जब तक उपकार करता है, तब तक मित्र होता है; मित्र उपकार के लक्षण वाला है।
english: As long as [it] helps, so long [it] is an ally; an ally [is] one having help as its mark.
notes: The subject of upakaroti is not stated (the controlled ally of unit 11). The closing iti after 'mitram' is an explanatory close of a definition; not rendered, glossed closing particle.
lines_deva: यावद् उपकरोति तावन् मित्रं भवति, उपकार.लक्षणं मित्रम् इति
lines_iast: yāvad upakaroti tāvan mitraṃ bhavati, upakāra.lakṣaṇaṃ mitram iti

words.gram: compound, m. nom. sg. (mahat + pres. part. upa-√kṛ)

hindi: दोनों वश में रहने वालों में भी महान् भोग वाला अनित्य, अथवा अल्प भोग वाला नित्य — “महान् भोग वाला अनित्य श्रेष्ठ है, महान् भोग वाला अनित्य थोड़े समय में बड़ा उपकार करता हुआ व्यय के बड़े स्थानों का प्रतिकार करता है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: Even among two controlled [allies], one of great enjoyment, inconstant, or one of small enjoyment, constant — “The one of great enjoyment, inconstant, is better; the one of great enjoyment, inconstant, helping greatly in a short time, remedies the great occasions of expenditure,” say the teachers.
notes: bhoga rendered literally 'enjoyment'; 'use, yield, extent of benefit' are possible (cf. glossary 3.8 bhoga = use). vyaya-sthāna = literally 'places/occasions of expenditure'. mahad-upakurvan: mahat is taken as adverbial/object 'greatly', both give the same sense. Sense of the either-or question closed by the first iti; not rendered.
lines_deva: वश्ययोर् अपि महा.भोगम् अनित्यम् अल्प.भोगं वा नित्यम् इति "महा.भोगम् अनित्यं श्रेयः, महा.भोगम् अनित्यम् अल्प.कालेन महद्.उपकुर्वन् महान्ति व्यय.स्थानानि प्रतिकरोति" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: vaśyayor api mahā.bhogam anityam alpa.bhogaṃ vā nityam iti "mahā.bhogam anityaṃ śreyaḥ, mahā.bhogam anityam alpa.kālena mahad.upakurvan mahānti vyaya.sthānāni pratikaroti" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

hindi: नित्य, अल्प भोग वाला श्रेष्ठ है।
english: The constant [one] of small enjoyment [is] better.
notes: No noun is stated; '[one]' is understood (the ally).
lines_deva: नित्यम् अल्प.भोगं श्रेयः
lines_iast: nityam alpa.bhogaṃ śreyaḥ

hindi: महान् भोग वाला अनित्य उपकार के भय से हट जाता है, अथवा उपकार करके वापस लेने का प्रयत्न करता है।
english: The inconstant [one] of great enjoyment goes away from fear of help, or, having helped, seeks to take back.
notes: upakāra-bhayāt is literally 'from fear of help'; whether the help is given or received is not stated. The object of pratyādātum is not stated.
lines_deva: महा.भोगम् अनित्यम् उपकार.भयाद् अपक्रामति, उपकृत्य वा प्रत्यादातुम् ईहते
lines_iast: mahā.bhogam anityam upakāra.bhayād apakrāmati, upakṛtya vā pratyādātum īhate

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. upa-√kṛ

hindi: नित्य, अल्प भोग वाला निरन्तरता से थोड़ा उपकार करता हुआ बड़े समय में बड़ा उपकार करता है।
english: The constant [one] of small enjoyment, through continuity, helping a little, helps greatly in a long time.
notes: mahatā kālena is the instrumental of time, 'in/over a long time'.
lines_deva: नित्यम् अल्प.भोगं सातत्याद् अल्पम् उपकुर्वन् महता कालेन महद् उपकरोति
lines_iast: nityam alpa.bhogaṃ sātatyād alpam upakurvan mahatā kālena mahad upakaroti

hindi: भारी उत्थान वाला महान् मित्र अथवा हल्के उत्थान वाला अल्प — “भारी उत्थान वाला महान् मित्र प्रताप उत्पन्न करने वाला होता है, और जब उठता है तब कार्य साधता है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: A great ally of heavy rising or a small one of light rising — “A great ally of heavy rising is a producer of splendour, and when [it] rises, then [it] accomplishes the task,” say the teachers.
notes: guru-samuttha / laghu-samuttha taken literally 'heavy-rising / light-rising' (i.e. slow or quick to rise, to take the field); the text does not say more. pratāpa = might, majesty. The first iti closes the either-or question; not rendered. Reviewer: pratāpa = splendour (glossary 7.4), not 'might'.
lines_deva: गुरु.समुत्थं महन् मित्रं लघु.समुत्थम् अल्पं वा-इति "गुरु.समुत्थं महन् मित्रं प्रताप.करं भवति, यदा च-उत्तिष्ठते तदा कार्यं साधयति" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: guru.samutthaṃ mahan mitraṃ laghu.samuttham alpaṃ vā-iti "guru.samutthaṃ mahan mitraṃ pratāpa.karaṃ bhavati, yadā ca-uttiṣṭhate tadā kāryaṃ sādhayati" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

hindi: हल्के उत्थान वाला अल्प श्रेष्ठ है।
english: The small [one] of light rising [is] better.
notes: No noun is stated; '[one]' is understood (the ally).
lines_deva: लघु.समुत्थम् अल्पं श्रेयः
lines_iast: laghu.samuttham alpaṃ śreyaḥ

hindi: हल्के उत्थान वाला अल्प मित्र कार्य के समय को निकलने नहीं देता, और दुर्बलता से इच्छानुसार भोग्य होता है, दूसरा नहीं, प्रकृष्ट भूमि वाला।
english: The small ally of light rising does not let the time of the task pass, and from weakness becomes [one] to be used as desired; not the other, [the one] of extensive territory.

text_flags.why: laghu is the word elsewhere in this chunk (units 18, 20); lagu is a likely typo

notes: prakṛṣṭa-bhauma is obscure: prakṛṣṭa 'excellent, extended, distant' and bhauma 'of the land'; rendered 'of extensive territory', literal alternatives noted. The same word occurs in unit 47. 'Becomes' translates bhavati; the ablative daurbalyāt is 'from weakness'.
lines_deva: लगु.समुत्थम् अल्पं मित्रं कार्य.कालं न-अतिपातयति दौर्बल्याच् च यथा.इष्ट.भोग्यं भवति, न-इतरत् प्रकृष्ट.भौमम्
lines_iast: lagu.samuttham alpaṃ mitraṃ kārya.kālaṃ na-atipātayati daurbalyāc ca yathā.iṣṭa.bhogyaṃ bhavati, na-itarat prakṛṣṭa.bhaumam

hindi: बिखरी हुई सेना वाला अथवा वश में न रहने वाली सेना वाला — “बिखरी हुई सेना को वापस समेटा जा सकता है, वश में होने से,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: [An ally] having scattered troops or having uncontrolled troops — “Scattered troops can be drawn back, because of being under control,” say the teachers.
notes: The bahuvrīhis have no stated noun; '[ally]' is understood from the context of the chapter. śakyam pratisaṃhartum is 'possible to be drawn back'; the infinitive is used passively. The first iti closes the either-or question; not rendered.
lines_deva: विक्षिप्त.सैन्यम् अवश्य.सैन्यं वा-इति "विक्षिप्तं सैन्यं शक्यं प्रतिसंहर्तुं वश्यत्वाद्" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: vikṣipta.sainyam avaśya.sainyaṃ vā-iti "vikṣiptaṃ sainyaṃ śakyaṃ pratisaṃhartuṃ vaśyatvād" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

hindi: वश में न रहने वाली सेना वाला श्रेष्ठ है।
english: [The one] having uncontrolled troops [is] better.
notes: No noun is stated; '[the one]' is understood (the ally).
lines_deva: अवश्य.सैन्यं श्रेयः
lines_iast: avaśya.sainyaṃ śreyaḥ

hindi: क्योंकि वश में न रहने वाले को साम आदि से वश में किया जा सकता है, कार्य में लगा हुआ दूसरा वापस समेटा नहीं जा सकता।
english: For the uncontrolled [one] can be made controlled by conciliation and the rest, not the other, engaged in a task, [can be] drawn back.
notes: 'Śakyam' is understood with the second clause (na itarat ... pratisaṃhartum): 'the other, engaged in a task, [cannot] be drawn back'. The translations keep the elliptic form. vyāsakta = engaged, absorbed (in a task).
lines_deva: अवश्यं हि शक्यं साम.आदिभिर् वश्यं कर्तुम्, न-इतरत् कार्य.व्यासक्तं प्रतिसंहर्तुम्
lines_iast: avaśyaṃ hi śakyaṃ sāma.ādibhir vaśyaṃ kartum, na-itarat kārya.vyāsaktaṃ pratisaṃhartum

hindi: पुरुषों में भोग वाला अथवा धन में भोग वाला मित्र — “पुरुषों में भोग वाला मित्र श्रेष्ठ है, पुरुषों में भोग वाला मित्र प्रताप उत्पन्न करने वाला होता है, और जब उठता है तब कार्य साधता है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: An ally of enjoyment in men or of enjoyment in money — “An ally of enjoyment in men is better; an ally of enjoyment in men is a producer of splendour, and when [it] rises, then [it] accomplishes the task,” say the teachers.

text_flags.why: likely typo: puruṣa is the word in the same quotation and in the first half of the unit; pruṣa is not a word

notes: puruṣa-bhoga is literally 'enjoyment (use) of men', understood as an ally whose enjoyment (benefit) consists of men; bhoga rendered as in unit 13. The first iti closes the either-or question and is not rendered.
lines_deva: पुरुष.भोगं हिरण्य.भोगं वा मित्रम् इति "पुरुष.भोगं मित्रं श्रेयः, प्रुष.भोगं मित्रं प्रताप.करं भवति, यदा च-उत्तिष्ठते तदा कार्यं साधयति" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: puruṣa.bhogaṃ hiraṇya.bhogaṃ vā mitram iti "puruṣa.bhogaṃ mitraṃ śreyaḥ, pruṣa.bhogaṃ mitraṃ pratāpa.karaṃ bhavati, yadā ca-uttiṣṭhate tadā kāryaṃ sādhayati" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

hindi: धन में भोग वाला मित्र श्रेष्ठ है।
english: An ally of enjoyment in money [is] better.
lines_deva: हिरण्य.भोगं मित्रं श्रेयः
lines_iast: hiraṇya.bhogaṃ mitraṃ śreyaḥ

hindi: क्योंकि धन से जुड़ाव नित्य है, सेना से कभी-कभी।
english: For connection with money [is] constant, with the army sometimes.
notes: yoga is rendered 'connection' (joining), not the 6.2 'acquisition'. daṇḍa = army here (the prakṛti sense, glossary 6.2/8.5/9.7: army); no Book 7 line exists; 'force' or 'punishment' are not intended. The verb of the second clause is understood.
lines_deva: नित्यो हि हिरण्येन योगः कदाचिद् दण्डेन
lines_iast: nityo hi hiraṇyena yogaḥ kadācid daṇḍena

hindi: सेना और अन्य कामनाएँ धन से प्राप्त की जाती हैं।
english: Both the army and other desires are obtained by money.
notes: daṇḍa = army, as in unit 29 (note there). The two ca are rendered 'both ... and'. The closing iti completes the reason and is not rendered. Printed 'hiraṇyena-anye' is the '-' join of two words (hiraṇyena, anye).
lines_deva: दण्डश् च हिरण्येन-अन्ये च कामाः प्राप्यन्त इति
lines_iast: daṇḍaś ca hiraṇyena-anye ca kāmāḥ prāpyanta iti

words.gloss: causing the remedy of all expenditure

hindi: धन में भोग वाला अथवा भूमि में भोग वाला मित्र — “धन में भोग वाला, गतिमान् होने से, सब व्ययों का प्रतिकार करने वाला है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: An ally of enjoyment in money or of enjoyment in land — “[The ally] of enjoyment in money, because of having movement, [is] one who causes the remedy of all expenditure,” say the teachers.
notes: gatimattva literally 'having movement/motion' (of money, i.e. mobility); no sense added. pratīkāra = remedy (glossary). The quoted sentence has no stated subject noun; '[The ally]' is understood.
lines_deva: हिरण्य.भोगं भूमि.भोगं वा मित्रम् इति "हिरण्य.भोगं गतिमत्त्वात् सर्व.व्यय.प्रतीकार.करम्" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: hiraṇya.bhogaṃ bhūmi.bhogaṃ vā mitram iti "hiraṇya.bhogaṃ gatimattvāt sarva.vyaya.pratīkāra.karam" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

hindi: क्योंकि “मित्र और धन भूमि के लाभ से होते हैं”, पहले कहा गया है।
english: For “ally and money arise from the gain of land” has been said before.
notes: Refers back to unit 2. The printed 'bhavata ity' is bhavataḥ iti.
lines_deva: मित्र.हिरण्ये हि भूमि.लाभाद् भवत इत्य् उक्तं पुरस्ताद्
lines_iast: mitra.hiraṇye hi bhūmi.lābhād bhavata ity uktaṃ purastād

hindi: इसलिए भूमि में भोग वाला मित्र श्रेष्ठ है।
english: Therefore an ally of enjoyment in land [is] better.
notes: The closing iti of the conclusion is not rendered.
lines_deva: तस्माद् भूमि.भोगं मित्रं श्रेय इति
lines_iast: tasmād bhūmi.bhogaṃ mitraṃ śreya iti

hindi: पुरुषों में भोग के बराबर होने पर पराक्रम, कष्ट सहने की क्षमता, अनुराग अथवा सब सेना का लाभ मित्र के कुल से विशेषता है।
english: When enjoyment in men is equal, valour, endurance of hardship, attachment, or the gain of all troops [is] the distinction from the ally's family.
notes: mitra-kulāt (ablative) is obscure: 'the distinction arising from / in comparison with the ally's family' are both possible; rendered literally. kleśa-sahatva = being able to bear hardship. bala = troops.
lines_deva: तुल्ये पुरुष.भोगे विक्रमः क्लेश.सहत्वम् अनुरागः सर्व.बल.लाभो वा मित्र.कुलाद् विशेषः
lines_iast: tulye puruṣa.bhoge vikramaḥ kleśa.sahatvam anurāgaḥ sarva.bala.lābho vā mitra.kulād viśeṣaḥ

words.gloss: the state of the object requested

hindi: धन में भोग के बराबर होने पर माँगे हुए अर्थ का भाव, प्रचुरता, प्रयास की अल्पता और निरन्तरता विशेषता है।
english: When enjoyment in money is equal, the state of the object requested, abundance, littleness of effort and continuity [are] the distinction.

text_flags.why: possible typo: prayasatā for prayāsatā (little effort)

notes: prārthita-arthatā is rendered literally ('state of [having] the requested object'); the sense (the object asked for being obtained) is not stated. alpa-prayasatā = 'having little effort'; ca joins the last item.
lines_deva: तुल्ये हिरण्य.भोगे प्रार्थित.अर्थता प्राभूत्यम् अल्प.प्रयसता सातत्यं च विशेषः
lines_iast: tulye hiraṇya.bhoge prārthita.arthatā prābhūtyam alpa.prayasatā sātatyaṃ ca viśeṣaḥ

hindi: इस विषय में यह है।
english: In this matter, this is.
notes: Formula introducing the verses that follow (units 38-49); '[verse]' is supplied because the verses follow in the next units.
lines_deva: तत्र-एतद् भवति
lines_iast: tatra-etad bhavati

hindi: नित्य, वश में रहने वाला, हल्के उत्थान वाला, पिता-पितामह का, महान् और द्वैधभाव से रहित — उत्कृष्ट मित्र छह गुणों वाला कहा जाता है।
english: Constant, controlled, of light rising, of father and grandfather, great, and non-dual — an excellent ally is called one having six qualities.
notes: The six qualities are the six adjectives of line a and the first of line b, counted as nitya, vaśya, laghu-utthāna, pitṛ-paitāmaha, mahat, advaidhya. advaidhya = literally 'non-doubleness'. The iti sums up the list and is not rendered. sampanna as in unit 7.
lines_deva: नित्यं वश्यं लघु.उत्थानं पितृ.पैतामहं महत्
अद्वैध्यं च-इति सम्पन्नं मित्रं षड्.गुणम् उच्यते
lines_iast: nityaṃ vaśyaṃ laghu.utthānaṃ pitṛ.paitāmahaṃ mahat
advaidhyaṃ ca-iti sampannaṃ mitraṃ ṣaḍ.guṇam ucyate

words.gloss: having a connection built up before

hindi: जो प्रयोजन के बिना स्नेह से रक्षित होता है और जो रक्षा करता है, जिसका सम्बन्ध पहले से बढ़ाया गया है, वह मित्र नित्य कहा जाता है।
english: [The ally] which, apart from a purpose, is protected out of affection, and which protects, having a connection built up before — that ally is called constant.
notes: ṛte artham is taken as 'apart from a purpose (artha)', i.e. without regard to gain. praṇaya has two senses, 'affection' and 'request' (glossary 5.2 has 'request' for Book 5): 'out of affection' chosen here, 'on request' is the alternative. upacita = built up, accumulated. The relatives yat ... yat have no stated noun; '[The ally]' is understood from mitram.
lines_deva: ऋते यद् अर्थं प्रणयाद् रक्ष्यते यच् च रक्षति
पूर्व.उपचित.सम्बन्धं तन् मित्रं नित्यम् उच्यते
lines_iast: ṛte yad arthaṃ praṇayād rakṣyate yac ca rakṣati
pūrva.upacita.sambandhaṃ tan mitraṃ nityam ucyate

words.gloss: of all, varied and great enjoyment

hindi: वश में रहने वाला तीन प्रकार का कहा जाता है: सर्व, चित्र और महान् भोग वाला; एक ओर से भोग करने वाला, दोनों ओर से, सब ओर से भोग करने वाला, और दूसरा।
english: The controlled [ally] is called threefold: of all, varied and great enjoyment; enjoying from one side, from both sides, enjoying from all sides, and another.
notes: Obscure. The compound sarva-citra-mahā-bhogam is read as a dvandva of three kinds of bhoga (all, varied, great) matching trividham; line b gives three kinds by direction of enjoyment, but with ubhayataḥ standing without bhogī and ca-aparam ('and the other') before sarvato-bhogi, the mapping between the two lines is uncertain. Rendered literally; gram of the compound is a guess.
lines_deva: सर्व.चित्र.महा.भोगं त्रिविधं वश्यम् उच्यते
एकतो.भोग्य् उभयतः सर्वतो.भोगि च-अपरम्
lines_iast: sarva.citra.mahā.bhogaṃ trividhaṃ vaśyam ucyate
ekato.bhogy ubhayataḥ sarvato.bhogi ca-aparam

words.gloss: retreating to its fort and forest

hindi: लेने वाला अथवा देने वाला भी अथवा — शत्रुओं में हिंसा से जीता है; मित्र नित्य, वश में न रहने वाला, और उसके दुर्ग और वन में हटने वाला।
english: Taking, or even giving, or — [it] lives among enemies by violence; an ally constant, uncontrolled, and retreating to its fort and forest.

text_flags.why: possible: the dot suggests a compound, but dātṛ and api are two words (sandhi dātry api)

notes: The second vā closes the alternatives (taking, or giving) and is rendered 'or' before the dash; the subject of jīvati is not stated. tad-durga-aṭavy-apasārin: apasārin = going away / retreating; the compound could also be 'having its fort and forest as place of retreat' (cf. glossary apasāra = place of retreat in 10.2). The sentence is elliptic.
lines_deva: आदातृ वा दात्र्.अपि वा जीवत्य् अरिषु हिंसया
मित्रं नित्यम् अवश्यं तद्.दुर्ग.अटव्य्.अपसारि च
lines_iast: ādātṛ vā dātr.api vā jīvaty ariṣu hiṃsayā
mitraṃ nityam avaśyaṃ tad.durga.aṭavy.apasāri ca

hindi: जो दूसरी ओर से विग्रह में पड़ा हुआ है अथवा हल्के व्यसन वाला ही है, और उपकार के लिए सन्धि करता है, वह मित्र वश में रहने वाला, अस्थिर है।
english: [The ally] which is assailed from another quarter, or indeed has a light calamity, and makes a treaty for help — that ally [is] controlled, unstable.
notes: vigṛhīta (vi-√grah) = one on whom war has been made / involved in hostility; rendered 'assailed'. sandhatte: object not stated ('makes a treaty [with him]'). vyasana = calamity (glossary 8.1). Order of vā and eva: 'light calamity indeed, or'.
lines_deva: अन्यतो विगृहीतं यल् लघु.व्यसनम् एव वा
सन्धत्ते च-उपकाराय तन् मित्रं वश्यम् अध्रुवम्
lines_iast: anyato vigṛhītaṃ yal laghu.vyasanam eva vā
sandhatte ca-upakārāya tan mitraṃ vaśyam adhruvam

words.gloss: changeable toward the one to be helped

hindi: यह मित्र, एक प्रयोजन से बँधा हुआ, तब उपकार्य के प्रति परिवर्तनशील और मित्रभावी, आपत्ति में द्वैधभाव से रहित है।
english: Bound by a single purpose, then changeable toward the one to be helped, and ally-natured, this ally is non-dual in adversity.
notes: Obscure. upakārya-vikārin read 'changing in regard to the one to be helped' (upakārya = one who is to be helped); the sense 'turning against' is not stated. mitra-bhāvin: bhāvin = having the nature of / tending to be; 'ally-natured'. atha rendered 'then'. Word order of the Hindi follows the English.
lines_deva: एक.अर्थेन-अथ सम्बद्धम् उपकार्य.विकारि च
मित्र.भावि भवत्य् एतन् मित्रम् अद्वैध्यम् आपदि
lines_iast: eka.arthena-atha sambaddham upakārya.vikāri ca
mitra.bhāvi bhavaty etan mitram advaidhyam āpadi

words.gloss: from being common with the enemy

hindi: मित्र-भाव से मित्र स्थिर है, शत्रु के साथ साझा होने से चल; किसी का नहीं, उदासीन; दोनों में वह दोनों के भाव वाला है।
english: From ally-nature the ally [is] firm, from being common with the enemy, shaky; [the one] of no one [is] neutral; of the two, that [one] is of both-nature.
notes: Verbless clauses with the copula supplied. na kasyacit udāsīnam: 'neutral [belongs] to no one'. dvayor ubhaya-bhāvi tat is read 'of the two (parties), that one is ubhaya-bhāvin'. Technical names of the classes: mitra-bhāvin, śatru-sādhāraṇa, udāsīna, ubhaya-bhāvin; the ones in units 45-48.
lines_deva: मित्र.भावाद् ध्रुवं मित्रं शत्रु.साधारणाच् चलम्
न कस्यचिद् उदासीनं द्वयोर् उभय.भावि तत्
lines_iast: mitra.bhāvād dhruvaṃ mitraṃ śatru.sādhāraṇāc calam
na kasyacid udāsīnaṃ dvayor ubhaya.bhāvi tat

hindi: जो मित्र विजिगीषु का अमित्र है, छिपाव में चला गया है, उपकार में लगा नहीं है, अथवा असमर्थ है, अथवा उपकार न करने वाला है — वह।
english: The ally which is an enemy of the conqueror, gone to concealment, not engaged in helping, or incapable, or non-helping — that [one].
notes: antardhitāṃ gatam: 'gone to concealment' (antardhitā, feminine abstract), taken literally. The list of unhelpful kinds is read as alternatives: enemy of the conqueror gone into concealment / not engaged in helping / incapable. vijigīṣu = the conqueror (glossary 6.2). Reviewer: vā kept where printed (before aśaktam and before anupakāri); the alternative reading 'tat anupakāri' as a predicate 'that is non-helping' is possible.
lines_deva: विजिगीषोर् अमित्रं यन् मित्रम् अन्तर्धितां गतम्
उपकारे ऽनिविष्टं वा-अशक्तं वा-अनुपकारि तत्
lines_iast: vijigīṣor amitraṃ yan mitram antardhitāṃ gatam
upakāre 'niviṣṭaṃ vā-aśaktaṃ vā-anupakāri tat

hindi: जो मित्र दूसरे के प्रिय, अथवा रक्षणीय, पूजनीय, अथवा सम्बद्ध को ही अनुगृहीत करता है, क्योंकि वह शत्रु के साथ साझा है।
english: The ally who favours [one] dear to the other, or [one] to be protected, venerable, or indeed connected — for that [ally] [is] common with the enemy.
notes: parasya is 'of the other' (glossary 9.2: para = the other, not 'enemy'). The objects (priyam, rakṣyam, pūjyam, sambaddham) are neuter accusatives without stated noun; '[one]' supplied.
lines_deva: प्रियं परस्य वा रक्ष्यं पूज्यं सम्बद्धम् एव वा
अनुगृह्णाति यन् मित्रं शत्रु.साधारणं हि तत्
lines_iast: priyaṃ parasya vā rakṣyaṃ pūjyaṃ sambaddham eva vā
anugṛhṇāti yan mitraṃ śatru.sādhāraṇaṃ hi tat

words.gram: n. nom. sg. ppp. caus. ava-√man

hindi: जो प्रकृष्ट भूमि वाला, सन्तुष्ट, बलवान् और आलसी दोनों है, यह उदासीन होता है, व्यसन के कारण अपमानित।
english: That which is of extensive territory, content, both strong and lazy — this becomes neutral, slighted through calamity.
notes: prakṛṣṭa-bhauma as in unit 21 (obscure). avamānitam is a separate qualifier of etat; the text has no conjunction, so none is added. vyasana = calamity (glossary 8.1).
lines_deva: प्रकृष्ट.भौमं सन्तुष्टं बलवच् च-आलसं च यत्
उदासीनं भवत्य् एतद् व्यसनाद् अवमानितम्
lines_iast: prakṛṣṭa.bhaumaṃ santuṣṭaṃ balavac ca-ālasaṃ ca yat
udāsīnaṃ bhavaty etad vyasanād avamānitam

hindi: जो शत्रु और नेता की वृद्धि का दुर्बलता से अनुसरण करता है, दोनों के द्वारा भी द्वेष न किया गया, उसे दोनों के भाव वाला जाने।
english: That which, from weakness, follows the growth of the enemy and of the leader, [and is] not hated even by both — one should know that as of both-nature.
notes: netṛ = the leader (the one who leads, i.e. the conqueror); not identified further. avidviṣṭam is read as an added qualifier without a conjunction; '[and is]' is bracketed in English. 'Not hated even by both' (ubhayasya api avidviṣṭam).
lines_deva: अरेर् नेतुश् च यद् वृद्धिं दौर्बल्याद् अनुवर्तते
उभयस्य-अप्य् अविद्विष्टं विद्याद् उभय.भावि तत्
lines_iast: arer netuś ca yad vṛddhiṃ daurbalyād anuvartate
ubhayasya-apy avidviṣṭaṃ vidyād ubhaya.bhāvi tat

hindi: जो कारण और अकारण से नष्ट हुए, कारण और अकारण से आए हुए मित्र की उपेक्षा करे, वह मृत्यु का आलिंगन करता है।
english: Whoever would neglect an ally — ruined through cause and non-cause, come through cause and non-cause — he embraces death.
notes: kāraṇa-akāraṇa is a dvandva 'cause and non-cause', i.e. ruined or arrived with or without a cause; rendered literally. samupekṣeta: opt. 'would/should neglect'.
lines_deva: कारण.अकारण.ध्वस्तं कारण.अकारण.आगतम्
यो मित्रं समुपेक्षेत स मृत्युम् उपगूहति
lines_iast: kāraṇa.akāraṇa.dhvastaṃ kāraṇa.akāraṇa.āgatam
yo mitraṃ samupekṣeta sa mṛtyum upagūhati

words.gloss: agreeing with the task, place and time

hindi: शीघ्र अल्प लाभ अथवा देर से महान् — “शीघ्र अल्प लाभ, कार्य, देश और काल के अनुरूप, श्रेष्ठ है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: A small gain quickly, or a great [one] after a long time — “A small gain quickly, agreeing with the task, place and time, [is] better,” say the teachers.
notes: In the Sanskrit vā stands after the first iti (iti vā); it is rendered 'or' between the alternatives. The first iti closes the either-or question and is not rendered. saṃvādaka = agreeing, accordant (with).
lines_deva: क्षिप्रम् अल्पो लाभश् चिरान् महान् इति वा "क्षिप्रम् अल्पो लाभः कार्य.देश.काल.संवादकः श्रेयान्" इत्य् आचार्याः
lines_iast: kṣipram alpo lābhaś cirān mahān iti vā "kṣipram alpo lābhaḥ kārya.deśa.kāla.saṃvādakaḥ śreyān" ity ācāryāḥ

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.
lines_deva: न-इति कौटिल्यः
lines_iast: na-iti kauṭilyaḥ

words.gloss: of the same nature as seed

hindi: देर तक न नष्ट होने वाला, बीज के समान धर्म वाला महान् लाभ श्रेष्ठ है; विपरीत होने पर पहला।
english: A great gain, not perishing for a long time, of the same nature as seed, [is] better; in the contrary [case], the former.
notes: The printed 'mahāml' is regular sandhi for mahān (before l); not flagged. sadharman = 'of the same dharma (property)'; bīja-sadharman is taken as 'like seed' (which keeps growing). pūrvaḥ = the former (the small quick acquisition of unit 50).
lines_deva: चिराद् अविनिपाती बीज.सधर्मा महाम्ल् लाभः श्रेयान्, विपर्यये पूर्वः
lines_iast: cirād avinipātī bīja.sadharmā mahāml lābhaḥ śreyān, viparyaye pūrvaḥ

words.gloss: intent on the accomplishment of his own purpose

hindi: इस प्रकार स्थिर लाभ में और लाभ के अंश में गुणों का उदय देखकर, अपने प्रयोजन की सिद्धि में तत्पर, सामवायिकों के साथ संहित होकर चढ़ाई करे।
english: Having seen thus the rise of qualities in a firm gain and in a share of gain, [one] intent on the accomplishment of his own purpose should march, allied with the associates.
notes: The subject of yāyāt is not stated (the conqueror); '[one]' is bracketed. sāmavāyika = associate (from samavāya, association); no further sense is given. guṇa-udaya = literally 'emergence of qualities/advantages'. yāyāt = should march (glossary 9.1).
lines_deva: एवं दृष्ट्वा ध्रुवे लाभे लाभ.अंशे च गुण.उदयम्
स्व.अर्थ.सिद्धि.परो यायात् संहितः सामवायिकैः
lines_iast: evaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhruve lābhe lābha.aṃśe ca guṇa.udayam
sva.artha.siddhi.paro yāyāt saṃhitaḥ sāmavāyikaiḥ
